text.p: The government of Benin, which is self-sufficient in cement, has raised the price of the commodity by almost 15 percent in response to a request from its three cement plants, which cited rising costs.
A statement from the West African nation's government said that from last Tuesday the price of a tonne of cement would rise 7,000 CFA francs ($12.40) to 54,500 CFA.
The three plants have an annual capacity of about 875,000 tonnes while officials say Benin's needs are just 500,000 tonnes.

A building boom has, however, boosted demand in Benin as in a string of other French-speaking West African countries following signs of economic recovery triggered by a 1994 devaluation of the CFA franc they share as a currency. ($1=565 CFA)
